sign board with cream lettering (front face)

answer.evidence: The sign is a tall, flat, front-facing board. At the top, rows 1-2 are a thin red strip, only about 2 rows, which is a rim and not a top surface. Rows 3-5 are a white panel, which is a vertical face. Rows 6-9 are darker shadow rows under the header. The board (rows 9-27) is a vertical face with cream lettering, and the grey base (rows 28-30) is also a vertical face. The silhouette widens only in the header (width 16 at rows 3-8) and the base. Neither has a front-edge line with a horizontal surface behind it, and there is no ellipse. Overall there is no real top surface, so the drawing is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin vertical sign, so I judged it mainly by eye. It has 8 visible tones per tile against 6 for bus-shelter-a, 12 for kiosk-a and 20 for vending-a, which puts it between the references and above the shelter. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the red body carries a highlight edge, mid and dark shading, a rim, and inner lettering strokes instead of one flat fill. The outline is a dark red-brown that leans toward the body colour. The 0% near-neutral share of dark edge pixels confirms there is no black sticker line. Its ramps are a little shallower, at about 4 steps, than the richest references (vending-a, kiosk-a), and the surface grain is modest. It still reads as the same quality as the shipped modern_city props and would sit next to them without looking flatter or thinner.

surfaces.part: top header box with white label
main sign board with cream lettering

answer.evidence: The sign is a tall front-facing board. Its top is a red header with a rounded silhouette (rows 0-2, width 12 then 14) and a white label on rows 3-5. The label is a vertical face, and rows 1-2 are only a 1-2 row rim. Rows 7-9 are dark shadow under the header, but there is no distinct edge line or horizontal plane. The lettered board (rows 10-27) and the grey base (rows 28-30) are flat vertical faces with no top surface and no receding side face. The structure matches the red front-elevation examples.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow red sign cabinet with a cream/yellow lettering panel. Its outline is a dark red-brown that leans toward the body colour, not neutral black. This matches the facts: 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, the same as all three references. It has no flat fills (0% near-flat coverage, the same as kiosk-a and vending-a, and better than bus-shelter-a at 9%). It shows 8 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). That is roughly mid-range for the set. The body has about 4 lightness steps (highlight edge, mid red, dark red, deep outline), against about 5 on the references. The lettering and the frame trim add detail, so it does not read as a flat sticker. It is a little simpler than vending-a but sits comfortably beside bus-shelter-a and kiosk-a, so it is acceptable for this chipset.
